newsitem.title: MONACO: Monaco celebrates, Rainier urges Albert to wed.
newsitem.headline: Monaco celebrates, Rainier urges Albert to wed.

text.p: Tiny Monaco launched a 10-month celebration of its 700th birthday on Wednesday as ageing Prince Rainier urged his son Albert to find a bride.

In interviews on the eve of the festivities, Rainier, 73, said the 38-year-old Albert -- one of the most eligible bachelors in the world -- had more work to do before he could succeed him and perhaps would have to marry first.
"He must sharpen his skills...I think he must gain some experience before he is completely ready to take over," Rainier told French television TF 1.

In a separate interview with France 2, he hinted that marriage and a family were part of the preparations for a handover, which he said could "perhaps, probably" take place before the end of the century.
"There is also the question of his marriage," Rainier said. "I would like him to take things in hand and at the same time start a family."

"There is no precise date...I do not know at all whether that will take place in the coming months, this year or in coming years," Albert confirmed in an interview aired on Monaco radio RMC just before the start of the festivities.

A morning mass at Monaco's cathedral launched official celebrations of the Grimaldi dynasty's 700th year in power over the Lilliput state, which has a population of just 30,000 and less than two square km (one square mile) of territory.
The mass was led by Archbishop Jean-Louis Tauran, the Vatican's emissary for relations with foreign states and the highest-ranking foreign dignitary at Wednesday's events.
Tauran may have been referring to the star-crossed but photogenic princely family when he spoke of an "uncertain world" and urged Monaco to head into the future armed with prayer.

This slice of Riviera real estate in the southeastern corner of France is best known for what is officially referred to as "the princely family" headed by the white-haired Rainier and including Princesses Caroline, 39, and Stephanie, 31, as well as the balding Albert.

Monaco first vaulted into the spotlight when Rainier married American film star Grace Kelly in 1956. Kelly died in a 1982 car crash but has remained Monaco's best-known symbol just as the rest of her family has remained a fixture in the world's glossy photo magazines and tabloids.
Following the mass, Rainier, the 29th Grimaldi to rule, unveiled a statue by Dutch sculptor Kees Verkade of Francois Grimaldi, the first in the family dynasty.

It was on January 8, 1297, that Francois, disguised as a monk, sneaked into the Genoese-controlled fortress, let in his own soldiers, and established the dynasty which claims to be the longest-serving in Europe.

"Honouring our ancestors, our land and our traditions: Isn't this the best way to reassure ourselves that we must continue on into the future ?," Rainier asked a crowd of a few thousand residents, tourists and other well-wishers rhetorically.

More than $200 million has been set aside for the birthday celebrations, which will include sporting events, car races, concerts, fireworks, art shows, plays -- and a meeting of the International Whaling Commission, intended to demonstrate the principality's commitment to environmental causes.
